payload.description:
## Context
The owner approved plan v4 on 2026-11-07. The scratchpad that held it is temporary, so its full text and the plan v3 phase detail it refers to are kept here. M0 shipped in 676caf2f and M1 in 258f4d0b. Milestone records M2b to M8 are siblings under basicly-gtb19bg.

## Plan v4

### basicly delivery overhaul: plan v4 (2026-11-07)

Change from v3: the four review skills come first. The work runs in milestones. Each milestone ends with a stop: gates green, commit, push, the owner reloads or restarts Claude, and the next milestone uses what the last one shipped. Its first use is its live test. Details per phase stay as in the plan v3 text below.

#### Milestone protocol (every milestone)
1. Done state: a command and the output it prints.
2. Gates for the touched files green; commit; push; CI on main green.
3. Stop message: what shipped, what to reload (skills: /reload-plugins or restart; hooks, agents, settings: restart).
4. After the restart, the first step uses the new capability on real work and records on its record: worked, or the defect it showed.
5. A defect found in use is fixed before the next milestone starts.
6. One /goal per milestone, so a planned stop never fights the stop hook.

#### Skill standard (every new and every existing skill)
- Follows the current Anthropic Claude Code skill guidelines, read from the live docs at M0 start through interface-facts and pinned on the record with the date.
- A skill is a folder, not one file: a short SKILL.md (what, when, the steps, links), with detail in references/, deterministic work in scripts/, templates and samples in assets/.
- SKILL.md stays short: the body links each reference one level deep; the description says what it does and when to use it, in user phrases.
- Every skill has evals.yaml: trigger phrases that must fire, near-miss phrases that must not, and task cases with checkable expected output.
- A gate in basicly skills-check refuses a new skill with no evals, a SKILL.md over the size cap, or a link to a missing file. Existing skills without evals are listed as debt that only goes down.

#### M0 review skills (basicly-gtb19bg.31 and its 3 children, plus a swarm child)
- swarm: the shared engine. N fresh agents, one lens each, a rubric, a reading list, a word cap. A missing report prints "not run". A finding with no path:line or command output is "unverified". Numbers, root causes and absence claims go to falsify-first by another agent. Output: verdict table plus numbered decisions with one recommendation each. It holds the rules the other three call.
- council: decides one question. Independent votes, no agent sees another's vote, majority plus dissent shown, a tie goes to the owner.
- teardown: finds every defect in one artifact. Lenses for correctness, security, poka-yoke, reuse and wording. Each finding gets a proposed fix and a severity.
- hill-climb: improves an artifact in graded rounds. Round 0 fixes the property list. The author never grades its own version. New lenses each round. Stop at two clean rounds or no property rising 1.0, cap 5.
- All four are catalog skills (every consumer gets them) built to the skill standard: SKILL.md plus references/, scripts/ where work is deterministic, assets/ for rubric and report templates, evals.yaml.
- skills-check gains the skill-standard gate first, so the four skills are built against it.
- Done: `basicly skills-check` passes with the new gate; the 4 skill folders appear in .claude/skills and .agents/skills; each skill's evals pass.
- STOP 1: commit, restart.

#### M1 use them on the skills (owner 2026-11-07: hill-climb 14 skills; rename, rewrite, restructure, merge or delete as results show; triage the rest)
- Triage (read-only, during the M0 CI wait): a swarm with lenses usage, simplicity and spec gives keep, improve, merge or delete for the 16 skills outside the climb list.
- Hill-climb in 4 clusters, so merge and delete decisions see the neighbours. Each cluster is one climb; reviewers grade the cluster and give per-skill findings.
  - A orchestration: swarm, council, hill-climb (teardown and falsify-first as neighbours).
  - B facts and diagnosis: interface-facts, root-cause, best-practices-audit (falsify-first as neighbour).
  - C planning and git: decompose-plan, work-tracker, worktree-isolation, conventional-commits.
  - D authoring and shell: skill-creator, catalog-authoring, no-comments, cli-tools.
- Properties (fixed in round 0): trigger-accuracy, brevity, clear-steps, poka-yoke, evals, facts, no-overlap.
- At most 8 agents at once: 2 clusters per wave with 4 reviewers each.
- Every changed skill leaves the debt list: evals.yaml with 3 task cases, graded by an independent agent.
- A merged or deleted skill gets a changelog fragment naming its replacement.
- council decides the 8 open plan decisions.
- Done: four climb state files with stop decisions; debt list shrunk by every climbed skill; triage verdicts applied or filed; CI green. STOP: reload.

#### M2 all skills to the standard
- Bring every existing skill (27 catalog skills on 2026-11-07) to the skill standard, worst first, each checked by teardown; the debt list reaches zero.
- Done: skills-check reports 0 skills in debt; every skill's evals pass.
- STOP: commit, reload.

#### M2b fast lane (plan-v3 Phase -1)
- Measure first; pre-commit keeps 7 hooks; other hooks become required CI jobs; record id only on PR and merge.
- Done: a one-file commit runs exactly 7 hooks in under 10 s.
- STOP 3: commit, restart (hooks load at process start).

#### M3 backlog and baseline (plan-v3 0.4, 0.5)
- council per batch labels or closes the 457 open records; baseline metrics recorded.
- Done: 0 open records without a phase label.

#### M4 dead weight (plan-v3 Phase 1)
- Done: per-PR CI median under 8 min; scripts with no caller deleted. STOP: reload.

#### M5 tracker (plan-v3 Phase 2)
- Design reviewed by teardown, then hill-climb, before code.
- Done: proof tests pass; real ledger migrated with fold equivalence. Release. STOP: restart.

#### M6 delivery process (plan-v3 Phase 3), one milestone each, a release when a consumer sees it
- M6a verification and two-axis code review skill
- M6b basicly ci init --provider github
- M6c AI review and security review in CI
- M6d risk tiers
- M6e merge queue
- M6f feature flags
- M6g staged release, rollback
- M6h end-to-end consumer transcript
- Each design goes through teardown before code; each diff goes through the M6a review before merge.

#### M7 design method (plan-v3 Phase 4)
- Done: ran on 3 sample tasks with recorded results. STOP: reload.

#### M8 cut and rewrite (plan-v3 Phase 5)
- Done: each cut step prints its expected output; always-on files under 600 words. Release.

#### Council on the 8 open decisions (2026-11-07, voters user, safety, skeptic; blind; swarm.py tally)
| # | Decision | Votes | Dissent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | fast-lane-next | 2 of 3 | skeptic: moving hooks to CI before intake shifts defects to slower feedback |
| 2 | in-git-conflict-free | 3 of 3 | none |
| 3 | native | 3 of 3 | none |
| 4 | humans-setting | 2 of 3 | skeptic: a setting that collapses two-person review is an escape hatch |
| 5 | every-commit | 2 of 3 | user: fewer refused commits with pr-and-merge |
| 6 | github-first | 3 of 3 | none |
| 7 | deprecate-now | 2 of 3 | skeptic: removes working machinery on a promise |
| 8 | wait-for-matchers | 3 of 3 | none |
Decision 5 differs from the v3 recommendation: keep the record id on every commit. The council recommends; the owner decides.


## Plan v3

### basicly delivery overhaul: plan v3 (2026-11-07)

Priorities: (1) task success: fast, correct, sound, through review and release; (2) a tracker that never conflicts; (3) a tested design method with mockups. Every phase is poka-yoke: wrong use is refused by name with the correct command. Every step has a size, a revert unit (one commit or one flag) and a done state that is a command plus the output it prints.

Round-1 grades (4 reviewers): coverage 6, order 6, poka-yoke 4-5, done states 4, speed 7, consumer risk 3-5, security 4, recovery 3, reuse 6, size 5.
Round-2 grades (3 new reviewers, lowest shown): coverage 7, order 4-7, poka-yoke 6, done states 5-6, speed 5-7, consumer risk 5-6, security 6-7, recovery 4-6, reuse 6-7, size 4-5. Round 3 runs as the first job of /hill-climb (0.3).

#### Phase -1: fast lane for this work (small; first, so building Phase 0 is fast)
-1.1 Measure first: `time git commit` on a one-file change, agent-hook latency per tool call, and the median of 5 pull_request CI runs, recorded on a research record.
-1.2 Pre-commit runs ruff, ruff format, pyright on changed files (added: no hook runs them today), secret-scan, identity-guard, tracker-path-scan and internal-info-scan. Every other pre-commit hook becomes a required CI job in the same commit. Agent hooks keep only safety guards; telemetry moves off the hot path. Done: `time git commit` on a one-file change lists exactly those 7 hooks and real time under 10 s; a test asserts the CI job lists every moved hook id; a revert of the commit restores the old hook list.
-1.3 A branch commit needs no record id; the id is required on the PR and the merge. Done: a test commits on a branch with no id and is accepted, and a merge without one is refused by name.

#### Phase 0: orchestration and intake (first; small to medium)
0.1 /swarm skill (.basicly/core/skills/swarm/, reuses the reviewer agent and lens_review.py markers). It refuses a lens with no rubric by name. Done (`pytest tests/test_swarm_skill.py -q` passes named cases): `/swarm <artefact> --lenses a,b,c` starts one fresh agent per lens with a rubric, a reading list and a word cap; a lens with no report prints `not run`; every finding carries path:line or a command and its output, else the synthesis marks it unverified; the synthesis is a verdict table plus numbered decisions with one recommendation each; numbers, root causes and absence claims go through falsify-first by an agent other than their author.
0.2 /hill-climb skill, built on /swarm. Done: round 0 fixes the artefact and a property list; reviewers grade, the author never grades its own version; new lenses each round; stop at two rounds with no finding of medium severity or above, or when no property rises 1.0, cap 5; each round prints its grade table; decisions go to the owner after the climb.
0.3 Tune both with themselves: hill-climb the two skill texts; evals.yaml covers 3 user trigger phrases, a missing report, an unverified finding and the stop rule; done when the evals pass N of N. Close basicly-gtb19bg.31.
0.4 Backlog intake by query, not by hand: bulk-label open, in_progress, blocked and deferred records by title rules, release stale claims, close by an age rule with a superseded-by reason, then review the remainder. Done: the count of records with no phase label is 0.
0.5 Task-success metrics on a closed research record, each with its source command: wall time per ordinary task, steps per bug fix, review rounds per change, pass after one round, commit hook time, per-PR CI time. Phase 3 must not raise wall time or steps for a tier-0 change; a check compares against this baseline.

#### Phase 1: CI speed and dead weight (small)
1.1 Consumer side of -1.2: install prints each moved hook and where it runs now, after one release of notice.
1.2 CI speed: per-PR runs Linux and affected tests; the three-platform pyright and the full suite run in the merge queue and on main. Done: per-PR quality-gates under 8 minutes.
1.3 Delete scripts with no code caller (about 1,300 lines, to be re-measured); done when `rg` for each deleted name across src, tests, .github and hooks returns 0 with one kept name as the positive control. Deprecate the loop, supervisor and factory commands now (warning names the replacement); removal follows 3.8.
1.4 Lefthook: keep our dispatcher, which has tool matchers; native `ai:` has none in v2.2.2. A recorded check re-tests the next lefthook release.

#### Phase 2: conflict-free tracker (large; before any parallel lanes; kit change that works with no engine)
2.1 Layout: one immutable file per event, named by the sha256 of its exact bytes, in a folder from the hash prefix: .basicly/ledger/events/ab/<hash>.json. No clock and no writer id in the path. The fold dedupes by event id (reuse ids.evidence_id and the existing fold dedupe), so the same logical event written twice with different timestamps counts once. Writes use O_EXCL; an existing file with the same bytes is success; temp files live under .git/, never in the ledger.
2.2 One layout resolver is the only reader; it checks that each file name equals the hash of its bytes and quarantines a mismatch; a gate refuses any other glob of .basicly/ledger. A ledger format version file; an older kit refuses a newer format by name and prints the upgrade command.
2.3 No commit on any branch, main included, modifies or deletes a tracked ledger file; only `basicly tracker pack` is exempt. The gate is a required CI check on the merge-base diff (local hooks are skipped by forge squash merges). `basicly rollback` and reverts exclude .basicly/ledger/. Packs are new immutable files that keep event ids; pack takes the queue lock, runs on a file-count threshold, and the fold dedupes across packs and loose files.
2.4 Proofs: two branches, two worktrees and a second clone each write; every merge order and an octopus merge with git merge-tree, with and without gitattributes (simulating a forge); pack while another branch appends; the same event on two branches folds once; concurrent writers in one checkout; a revert on main; two packs on two machines; read time for 100,000 events under 2 s on Linux and Windows as a pytest bound; the old layout still reproduces its conflict as the control.
2.5 Migration (its own phase-sized step): `basicly tracker migrate --dry-run` first; legacy logs stay readable and old-format appends on open branches are accepted and packed on main; fold equivalence (record count and field hash) before and after on the real ledger; an interrupted migration test; a tagged pre-migration commit as the rollback point; migrate refuses to finish while an open branch predates it and lists each branch by name; legacy files deleted only after that list is empty; the upgrade test (a v0.42 consumer fixture with an open branch) is a step here with a done command.

#### Phase 3: the delivery process (priority 1; three worktree lanes after Phase 2)
3.1 Verification: the agent shows output; a fresh-context two-axis review (standards and spec, never merged) before the PR, built on the existing reviewer agent and /swarm, not a new reviewer. Tier 0 gets one review, in CI only.
3.2 CI by skill and command: `basicly ci init --provider github` first; bitbucket-pipelines.yml, bamboo-specs/bamboo.yaml and GitLab as separate records; Jenkins, Azure DevOps and CircleCI listed for later. Generated files: permissions empty at the top, never pull_request_target, actions pinned by full SHA, no secrets for fork PRs; a check refuses a file that breaks any of these by name; never overwrites an existing file without --force; plain `basicly install` never writes CI files.
3.3 AI review and security review in CI: claude-code-action with the code-review plugin and the security review action, same-repo PRs only, key in a secret or OIDC; a check refuses secrets in any job a fork PR triggers; every finding answered before merge; no key means the job fails as not run, never green.
3.4 Risk tiers (extends classify.py; off by default for consumers; `[review] humans` sets how many people exist, so a solo maintainer's tier 2 becomes 1 with a logged note): paths, size and a sensitive-path list read from the base branch set none, one or two approvals; editing the list itself needs two people; unknown paths or a classifier error mean two; enforced through forge branch protection and CODEOWNERS with stale approvals dismissed; an agent or bot approval never counts.
3.5 Merge queue (extends merge.merge_queue and `basicly worktree merge-queue`; designed before the pack step is frozen): provider auto, github, bitbucket or basicly, read at landing time; `auto` refuses to land when it finds no queue until `basicly` is set explicitly; the basicly queue refuses while a forge queue is on, and an unreachable forge API or a missing token counts as on (refuse); the proof that checks ran is a required CI status on the exact tree SHA, never local output; it lands with --ff-only only after checks ran on the exact tree; across machines it holds a lock ref on origin by compare-and-swap, as a lease with owner and expiry, with `basicly queue unlock --reason`; with no branch protection it says it is advisory.
3.6 Feature flags (native, no new dependency): `basicly flag add <name> --owner --expires --removal <id>` writes a flag registry; code reads flags through one small module with an OpenFeature-shaped interface; a missing flag or a provider failure means off and a log line; security flags cannot be overridden by environment; a CI gate fails on an expired flag or a flag with no removal record; a skill teaches release and deploy behind a flag.
3.7 Release and recovery (extends release.py; after 3.6): staged channels; a fix-forward-or-roll-back skill with a decision rule; `basicly rollback` turns a flag off or reverts a release through the same queue, with an emergency path behind an explicit flag and a logged reason; a rollback drill runs in CI on each minor release.
3.8 Retire what the new process replaces: the loop phases, the verify and validate gates and the reviewer and validator agents that it supersedes, each deprecated for one release with a warning naming its replacement.
3.9 End-to-end proof: one consumer repo runs PR, review, approval, queue, release, flag-off and rollback, recorded as a transcript.

#### Phase 4: solution design (medium; reuses the designer agent and validate-as-consumer)
4.1 design skill: grill the user (numbered questions, each with a recommended answer), then a design doc: problem, critical user journeys, options with failure modes, Zero-Decision implementation plan, agreed test seams, tickets sized to one fresh context.
4.2 UI: text wireframes, then an HTML mock rendered and screenshotted at every claimed viewport, judged against the journeys.
4.3 Review by /hill-climb with rubric lenses: zoom-out, implementation readiness, UX.
4.4 Tested: run the method on three sample tasks against a plain-agent baseline and record rework, findings and time.

#### Phase 5: cut and rewrite (large; one record per deleted check)
5.1 A check is deleted only when the gate-failure history shows no failure on main in the last 60 days and no regression test cites it; the deleting commit cites that history. Useful scripts are rewritten, not kept as they are.
5.2 Skills: user-phrase triggers, under 500 words, positive instructions, a suggested-skills handover; always-on files under 600 words; a wording gate refuses a term defined two ways across skills and always-on files, and trigger evals catch a skill that fires on the wrong phrase.
5.3 Engine removals already planned under basicly-gtb19bg.30.

#### Cross-cutting
- Every done state is a command plus its expected output; phases without one are not started.
- Every claim from a swarm carries path:line or a command; the author never grades its own work.
- Upgrade test: install over a v0.42 consumer fixture with an open branch before every release that changes a consumer.
- basicly's own changes ship behind flags where they change consumer behaviour.
- Dependency graph: -1 first; 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, then 0.4 and 0.5; 1 next; 2 before parallel lanes; 3 and 4 in parallel worktrees (3 owns src/basicly/merge.py, release.py, classify.py and CI templates; 4 owns skills and agents); 3.6 before 3.7; 5.2 after 0 and 4.
- Release after each phase that changes what a consumer sees.

payload.title: M5: ship the conflict-free tracker design

payload.text: [owner requirement 2026-11-10] The owner called this extremely important for the next session. The work tracker, and above all the standalone tracker kit, must serve a team of many developers and agents on one repository and never end in a merge conflict. Four things must never happen. 1: two pull requests are open, both edit the same tracker file, one is merged, and the other gets a merge conflict and cannot be merged. 2: several agents on one machine and one repository write the same tracker file, overwrite each other and fight over it, which can corrupt the file and cause resolution work. 3: the tracker is out of sync with the actual code. 4: the tracker state is not shared with the other developers in time. Each of the four needs a proof test in the design of this milestone (plan v3 step 2.4 already lists merge-order and concurrent-writer proofs; cases 3 and 4 have no proof there yet). Evidence from this session: the forge ignores gitattributes for mergeability, so only disjoint paths prevent case 1.

[order 2026-11-10] The owner moved this milestone ahead of M3 and M4. New order after the model roles work: M5 conflict-free tracker (this record), then M3 backlog labels (basicly-gtb19bg.41), M4 CI dead weight (basicly-gtb19bg.42), M6 delivery process (basicly-gtb19bg.44). M2b (basicly-gtb19bg.40) is not in the chain: the owner approved skipping its hook move, and its commit time target is met for Markdown.

[owner constraint 2026-11-10] No design with one file per record or one file per event. The owner named the beans tracker as the counter-example: its Markdown file per story leaves a repository with more tracker files than code. A backlog can pass 10000 stories, and 10000 tracker files is a no-go. This rules out plan v3 step 2.1 as written (one immutable file per event, named by its hash). The owner asks for a smarter, new solution. So the design must meet both bars at once: the four never-events of the earlier comment, and a file count that stays small and does not grow with the number of records or events. Design inputs to test first, none decided: (a) one append-only shard per writer or branch, folded into a few packed files on the main branch by one serialized step, so the file count follows open branches, not records; (b) tracker state kept outside the pull request tree, in its own git ref, written with compare-and-swap and merged by the tool, so no pull request ever holds a tracker file; (c) a hybrid of both. Before any novelty claim, check prior art with falsify-first: git-bug and git notes keep issue data in git refs.

[owner constraint 2026-11-10, third] No hidden storage. Tracker data must not live in git refs, git notes or any place outside the normal working tree. The owner's reasons: such data is invisible in GitHub and Bitbucket and in ordinary git tools, a person finds it only when they already know where to look, and a person who wants to remove the tracker from a repository would not know the data exists. This rules out design input (b) of the earlier comment and the ref half of input (c). What remains to design: visible, ordinary tracked files in the working tree, few in number, whose count does not grow with records or events, and which two open pull requests and several local writers can change without a merge conflict. The forge ignores gitattributes for mergeability, so a union merge driver is not an answer either. Input (a), one append-only file per writer or branch folded on main by one serialized step, is the only earlier input still standing, and its fold step is the open risk.

[owner correction 2026-11-10, fourth] The owner corrected the agent: 'few visible tracked files in the working tree' was a constraint the agent put on itself, not one the owner set. The solution space is open. A dedicated backlog repository, a repository within a repository, a package, an app, a service or anything else is acceptable. The owner's method: expand the solution space first, then contract it to the one solution that fits. He asks for an innovative, smart solution that nobody has built. The owner's constraints stay exactly these: (1) the four never-events; (2) not thousands of tracker files in the code repository, since a backlog can pass 10000 stories; (3) nothing hidden: a person must see the tracker data in ordinary tools such as GitHub and Bitbucket, and must be able to find and remove it without inside knowledge, so git refs and git notes are out. The earlier comment's last sentences, which named one remaining input, are withdrawn: they contracted the space too early. Next session: first a wide survey of solution families with prior art checked, each scored against the three constraints, then the contraction by hill-climb, then a design, then code.

[survey 2026-11-10] Three Opus researchers, 30 tool calls each, 79 calls used. 17 families scored against N1-N4, C2, C3. Eliminated by C3 (hidden or not on the forge): git refs and notes (git-bug, Radicle, git-appraise, git-dit), Dolt and beads (refs/dolt/data), Fossil tickets, hosted database, CRDT sync app, Linear. Eliminated by N1: fixed buckets, CRDT file in repo, submodule, subtree. Eliminated by N2: package or artifact store. Eliminated by N3 plus Bitbucket: forge issues (Bitbucket Cloud removed its issue API on 2026-08-20). Today's design (shard per branch, manual compact) fails N4 by structure and N1 by basicly-qlf1ed3. Standing: separate backlog repository with compare-and-swap push; visible orphan branch (C2 is an owner call); status derived from code commit trailers as an N3 layer; local lock or daemon as an N2 layer. No prior art combines a separate repository, compare-and-swap push and a code link (two searches, not proof). N3 has no enforcing prior art in any family. Awaiting owner review before hill-climb.

[hill-climb 2026-11-10] Result stored on basicly-gtb19bg.58 (research, open because closing needs the readiness review). 5 rounds stopped at the cap; final lowest grades n1 7, n2 7, n3 5, n4 6, c2 9, c3 7, operability 5. Contraction: separate backlog repository, one linear event log with one file per writer, first claim in log order wins, close derived from closes/refs/none declarations on the code default branch. No design yet. Owner decisions open: (1) is an orphan tracker branch in the code repository allowed under C2 and C3 (the round 5 Opus reviewer rates it as good and simpler); (2) cut the first release to the core and defer hardening; (3) BACKLOG.md required or optional. Round 5 findings are not yet verified by a fresh agent.

[owner decisions 2026-11-11] (a) An orphan tracker branch in the code repository is not allowed: C3 bans every git ref; the separate backlog repository stands. (b) Core first: the first release holds the event log, the first-claim rule, closes/refs/none declarations with revert handling, fsck --code and the migration; identity checks, signing, CODEOWNERS, --restore, takeover and the 7-day expiry are deferred. (c) BACKLOG.md is optional: raw per-writer event files on the forge satisfy C3; the board or a CLI view renders them.

acceptance: When a vault clone holds a genesis, format, batch or archive commit of the shape design v8 revision 3 section 2.5 names, vault-check shall count it valid.

When a vault commit has any other shape, a batch line names a writer other than its segment writer, or a line is changed or removed, vault-check shall quarantine that commit alone, report it with its id and the rule it breaks, and keep every later valid commit.
When a vault holds a valid ended event, vault-check shall count nothing after it.

Proof T-fork-shapes: input a local bare vault with one genesis, two batches, one forged-writer line, one web-edited line, one bypass merge and one ended event followed by a batch; action vault-check; pass when exactly the forged, edited, merge and after-ended commits are quarantined and the other commits are valid.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py vault-check vault.git` prints each commit as valid or quarantined with its rule
tasks.title: S2b: check vault commit shapes and quarantine any other commit

acceptance: When two sessions claim one record in a vault, the fold shall make the claim in the earlier valid commit the holder and report the later one as void.
When a writer who is not the holder writes unassign for a record, the fold shall void that event and keep the holder.
When a fold meets an unknown kind that carries fold true, the fold shall keep the line and holder commands on that record shall refuse and name the upgrade.
When a config event changes a status set, the fold shall read each earlier event under the configuration in force at its position.
Proof T-exclusive-fold: input a vault with 3 writers and 8 sessions claiming one record in 11 batches; action vault-show; pass when exactly one holder is shown and 10 claims are listed as void.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py vault-show vault.git demo-a1b2` prints the holder and the void claims
tasks.title: S2b: fold a vault into records where the first valid claim wins

acceptance: When a tracker kit module outside the adapter and transport layers reads os.environ or imports subprocess, socket or http, the kit-boundary gate shall refuse it by module and line.
When holders.py, writers.py and events.py run, they shall take the environment values they need as arguments from the adapters, with today's ledger commands unchanged for the user.
Proof T-layers: input the kit tree plus one seeded module that reads os.environ; action the kit-boundary gate; pass when only the seeded module is refused and the shipped tree passes.
tasks.demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_kit_boundary.py -q` passes and refuses a seeded os.environ read in a kit module
tasks.title: S2b: refuse environment reads and processes below the adapter layer

acceptance: When registry init runs on an empty repository, the tracker shall push a genesis commit with vault.toml of kind registry, FORMAT.md, reader.py and README.md.

When project add runs, the tracker shall refuse a vault equal to the code repository by normalized host and path or by root commit, refuse a non-empty vault whose genesis names another project, push project-register like a claim, and write the vault genesis; a rerun shall continue at the first missing step.
When a second project registers a prefix the registry already owns, the tracker shall refuse it and name the owning project.
When member add runs, the tracker shall append a person event, and member list shall show it.

Proof T-register: input local bare registry and vault repositories; action registry init, member add, project add twice with one prefix clash and one crash after the registration push; pass when the clash is refused by name, the rerun completes the vault genesis, and the registry folds to one project.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py project add --name demo --prefix demo --vault vault.git --code code` exits 0 and a rerun with the same prefix for another vault exits non-zero naming the owner
tasks.title: S2c: create a registry and register a project with its vault

acceptance: When attach runs in a code repository whose tracker.toml names a registry uid, the tracker shall accept a registry URL only when its genesis uid matches, clone the vault bare into the machine state folder, reuse writer.id across reclones, install version-marked hooks and print the session rule in use.
When a piece is missing (tool, registry URL, vault access, hook), attach shall refuse with the exact command that fixes it.
When an agent marker variable is set and no agent session id exists, a claim session lookup shall refuse the machine person session.

Proof T-newcomer-local: input a code repository with tracker.toml and local bare registry and vault; action attach in a fresh state folder, then reclone; pass when the writer id is unchanged after reclone, the hooks carry the version marker, and each removed prerequisite is refused with its command.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py attach --registry registry.git` in a code repository exits 0 and prints the session rule and the clone path

Confirmed breaks and smallest fixes:
C1 (N4): in a core-only build, bulk events and reader fetches have no bounded trigger, because the Stop, SessionEnd, prompt and SessionStart hooks are in S6. Fix: move those share-and-fetch hooks into S3 and gate S7 on T-bulk and T-visible (core scope change).

C3 (N4): rollback pushes ended to the vault only and the core registry has no ended, so shares after rollback never reach the ledger. Fix: ended in S2c, registry first, any ended stops shares and keeps the queue (clarification).

acceptance: When a tracker command first needs a vault, the tracker shall clone it bare into the vault's folder under the machine state folder with mode 0700 and fetch with the refspec +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main.
While one command fetches a clone, any other fetch of that clone shall wait on the clone's one fetch lock.
If a fetch fails, the tracker shall retry it once, then use the last fetched state and print its age.
When a fetch succeeds and every new first-parent commit passes vault-check, the tracker shall move refs/basicly/seen to the fetched head.
Proof T-refspec: input a fixture bare vault and a fresh bare clone; action push one batch commit to the vault, then fetch; pass when refs/remotes/origin/main and refs/basicly/seen equal the new head.

Proof T-fetch-lock: input one clone and two concurrent fetches, one stalled 5 s by an injected git runner; action run both; pass when neither prints cannot lock ref and the head ref never moves backwards.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py fetch --vault vault.git` prints the clone path, the head and the data age
tasks.title: S3: clone a vault bare into the machine state folder and fetch it under one lock

acceptance: When any tracker command writes an event for a vault, the tracker shall pass the event through the standard-library redactor shipped in the kit, then append it to queue.jsonl beside the clone under LedgerLock with fsync.
When the redactor finds a credential shape or an absolute path in any event field, it shall replace it before the event reaches the queue.
When a write is queued, the command shall print queued with the event count and the oldest age, and name the next command or hook that shares it.
Where CI or BASICLY_TRACKER_EPHEMERAL is set, the adapter shall request an immediate share for every write.
If the queue tail is torn, the tracker shall cut it back under LedgerLock and report the missing event.

Proof T-redact: input a fixture vault clone and one comment whose text holds a fake token assembled at run time and an absolute home path; action write it through the kit CLI; pass when neither string appears in queue.jsonl and the redacted markers do.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py comment demo-a1b2 --vault vault.git --text 'see <redacted:posix-home-path>'` prints queued (1 events and the queue line holds no home path
tasks.title: S3: queue redacted events beside the vault clone

acceptance: When a share runs, the tracker shall take the share lock, fetch, drop queued events whose ids are valid on the head, build one single-parent batch commit on the head with hash-object, a temporary index, write-tree and commit-tree, and push it plainly.
When the push is refused, a bulk share shall fetch and rebuild at most 5 times; an urgent share shall retry until its deadline passes.
When the push succeeds, the tracker shall move refs/basicly/seen, then remove the shared events from the queue under LedgerLock.
If the fetched head holds a valid ended event, the share shall push nothing, keep the queue and print the ended reason and successor.
When a share crashes at any step, the next sync shall leave each event in the vault exactly once.
Proof T-share-smoke: input a fixture bare vault and 3 clones; action write 100 events in each clone and sync all clones concurrently; pass when the vault folds to 300 events, each exactly once.
Proof T-writers: input 16 local processes and 50 clones of one fixture vault; action write 10,000 events and sync until every queue is empty; pass when each event id appears exactly once.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py sync --vault vault.git` prints shared with the event count and the new head
tasks.title: S3: share the queue as one plumbing commit on the fetched head

acceptance: When a fetched head's first-parent chain lacks the refs/basicly/seen tip, the tracker shall store the old tip as refs/basicly/retracted/N, refuse every share and name basicly-tracker fsck --repair.

When fsck --repair runs, it shall re-queue own lines from retracted refs as they were, put other writers' lines in one requeue event that keeps their ids and changes no holder, and write claim-lost for each claim that no longer holds.
When fsck --accept-rewrite names the head with --purge, the tracker shall drop the retracted refs and allow shares again.
When reclone runs, it shall copy refs/basicly/seen and every retracted ref into the new clone and keep writer.id.

Proof T-seen: input clone B that fetched a commit by writer W, then a force-push that removes it from a fixture vault; action B shares, then runs fsck --repair, then reclone; pass when the share is refused naming fsck --repair, the repair restores W's lines in one requeue event, and reclone keeps both refs.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py fsck --repair --vault vault.git` prints the requeued and claim-lost counts and the next share succeeds
tasks.title: S3: refuse to share after a retraction and repair it with fsck --repair

acceptance: When the SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit hook runs, the tracker shall fetch with a 3 s deadline at most once every 20 s and run a share only when the bulk slot is due.
When the Stop or SessionEnd hook runs, the tracker shall share the whole queue.
When status runs, it shall print the fetch age, the last shared event per writer and the queued count and age, without a network call.
The S3 slice shall merge only when T-share-smoke, T-writers, T-seen, T-refspec, T-fetch-lock, T-redact, T-agents, T-no-code-write and T-visible pass.

Proof T-agents: input 8 sessions in 3 worktrees of one code clone attached to a fixture vault; action write 1,000 events and fire Stop in every session; pass when each event lands once and no lock wait exceeds 1 s.
Proof T-no-code-write: input a code clone attached to a fixture vault; action 1,000 tracker writes and hooks; pass when git status --porcelain of the code clone is empty.

Proof T-visible: input clones A and B of a fixture vault; action A writes a comment and fires Stop, B fires SessionStart then runs status; pass when B shows the comment and the printed data age is under 30 s.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py hook stop --vault vault.git` exits 0 with an empty queue and `status` prints the data age
tasks.title: S3: share and fetch from the SessionStart, prompt, Stop and SessionEnd hooks

acceptance: This child starts only after record basicly-2qyhk3z is done.
When claim runs, the tracker shall spend one 30 s deadline over every git call including the fetch, giving each call only the time that remains.
If the id or session is missing, claim shall exit 1 and print the fix; if git ls-remote gives no answer within 5 s, it shall exit 5, queue nothing and print the ls-remote command.
When the fetched fold shows the record held by this session, claim shall exit 7; held by another session, it shall exit 3 with no push and print the take command.
When the claim lands as the first valid claim, claim shall exit 0; when another claim lands first, exit 3; when the deadline passes first, exit 4 and print unsettled with --wait and --cancel.
If an internal error occurs, claim shall exit 6 with no traceback and print the log path and sync.
While a claim is urgent, its share shall retry refused pushes until the 30 s deadline passes, not for a fixed count.
Proof T-exclusive: input 3 clones and 8 sessions in one clone of a fixture vault; action all claim one record at once; pass when exactly one exits 0 and the rest exit 3.
Proof T-urgent-retry: input 13 clones and injected push latency; action 13 claims in one second; pass when no claim stops before 13 attempts unless its deadline passed.
Proof T-claim-burst: input 13 claims in one second with one fetch stalled 40 s; action run them; pass when every command answers within 30 s and every claim ends 0 or 3 within 60 s.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py claim demo-a1b2 --vault vault.git` exits 0 and a second session's claim of the same record exits 3 naming the take command
tasks.title: S4: claim a record within one 30 s deadline and answer with a named exit code

acceptance: While a claim is unsettled, the tracker shall never report it as held, and the next tracker command or hook shall retry its share.
When claim --wait runs, the tracker shall wait until the claim lands and exit 0 or 3.
When claim --cancel runs, the tracker shall take the share lock, fetch, and drop the queued claim, or unassign it if it landed.
When an unsettled claim is 10 minutes old at the end of a fetch, the tracker shall expire it the same way as --cancel.

Proof T-expiry: input an injected clock and two unsettled claims aged 10 minutes, one landed and one not; action run a fetch; pass when the unlanded claim is dropped from the queue and the landed one is unassigned.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py claim demo-a1b2 --cancel --vault vault.git` exits 0 and status shows no holder and no queued claim
tasks.title: S4: settle, wait for, cancel or expire an unsettled claim

acceptance: When claim --take runs with --reason, the tracker shall push the take as urgent, log it, and show taken by name and reason to the old holder at its next hook or command.
If the claim was made in the last 30 minutes, claim --take shall refuse unless --force is given.
When claim --take runs without --reason, the tracker shall take only from a same-writer session idle for 30 minutes in sessions.json, and refuse otherwise naming --reason.
When unassign runs from a session that is not the holder, the tracker shall refuse it and name the holder.
When unassign --to names a holder that has written to this vault, the tracker shall hand the claim to it in one urgent event.

Proof T-take: input a fixture vault with a claim held by session S1 on writer W; action S2 on W takes without a reason after 30 idle minutes, S3 on another writer takes with a reason, S1 unassigns, then the holder unassigns --to S1; pass when the takes succeed, the non-holder unassign is refused, and S1 holds the record at the end.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py claim demo-a1b2 --take --reason 'machine lost' --vault vault.git` exits 0 and show prints the new holder and the reason
tasks.title: S4: take a held claim with a reason and hand one over with unassign --to

acceptance: When the claim load script runs, it shall drive the real claim command from 52 sessions on 13 clones of a local bare vault with 1.5 s push and 0.5 s fetch latency injected, time scaled 4 times, and print p95, p99, exit code counts, holders per record and push attempts per minute.
The S4 slice shall merge only when T-claim-gate, T-exclusive, T-urgent-retry, T-claim-burst and T-expiry pass.

Proof T-claim-gate: input 52 sessions on 13 machines, time scaled 4 times, seeds 1 to 3, 30 scaled minutes each; action run the claim load script; pass when every claim ends 0 or 3 within 60 s, no claim exits 4, each record has one holder and p95 is at most 10 s.
tasks.demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/claim_load.py --sessions 52 --machines 13 --scale 4 --seed 1` prints p95 at most 10 s and one holder per record
tasks.title: S4: measure claim latency under 52 sessions and gate the S4 merge on it

acceptance: When a commit message carries no record id and no Record: none line, the commit-msg hook shall refuse the commit and print the claim command and Record: none.
When the message starts with git-generated Merge, Revert with a quote, fixup! or squash!, the hook shall accept it, and a revert or fixup shall inherit the named commit's record id.
When the message has no id and the session holds exactly one claim, the hook shall append that record id in parentheses to the subject.
When the named record is not held by this session or its claim is unsettled, the hook shall accept the commit and warn with the claim command.
While the vault cannot be reached, the hook shall record a local miss event in the queue.
The hook body shall be installed by attach, record basicly-gtb19bg.43.9.

Proof T-hook: input messages with an id, with Record: none, with nothing, Merge, Revert with a quote and fixup!; action run the hook on each; pass when only the message with nothing is refused and the revert inherits the id.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py commit-msg tests/fixtures/no-id-message.txt` exits 1 and prints Record: none and the claim command
tasks.title: S5a: refuse a commit with no record id in the commit-msg hook

acceptance: When fsck --code runs, the tracker shall fetch the code default branch within a bounded deadline, or use the local state and print its age.
When the code default branch holds a commit naming a record id, fsck --code shall store one link event whose id is a content hash, so a second run adds nothing.
When the code default branch holds a merged commit with no record id or a Record: none commit, fsck --code shall store one miss event and list it.
When a commit says closes with a record id or reverts a linked commit, fsck --code shall list a suggestion and change no status.
When a record is in progress with no code activity, or a claim is stale, fsck --code shall list it.
When SessionStart fires or a share succeeds, the tracker shall run fsck --code on the local code clone.
The S5a slice shall merge only when T-hook, T-audit and T-link pass.

Proof T-audit: input a code clone with a commit made with --no-verify, a direct push with no id and a commit saying closes a record id; action fsck --code; pass when there is one miss for each of the first two and one suggestion for the third.
Proof T-link: input a code clone with two commits naming one record; action fsck --code twice; pass when the vault holds two link events after the first run and no new event after the second.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py fsck --code --vault vault.git` lists misses and suggestions and a second run stores no new event
tasks.title: S5a: audit the code default branch with fsck --code and store link and miss events

acceptance: When migrate --from ledger runs with --freeze, the tracker shall freeze the ledger, import its events in today's fold order keeping ids, verify the event count and digest against the vault fold, and write the cutover files.
When migrate runs with --preview, it shall print the counts and digest and change nothing.
When migrate is rerun after a crash at any step, it shall resume at the first missing step and import no event twice.
When migrate --abort runs before cutover, the tracker shall unfreeze the ledger.
If the count or digest differs, migrate shall refuse cutover and name both values.

Proof T-migrate: input a copy of a ledger with forks, aliases and closed records and an empty fixture vault; action migrate --freeze with a crash injected after the import, then rerun; pass when the vault fold equals the ledger fold record by record and the digest matches.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py migrate --from ledger .basicly/ledger --vault vault.git --freeze` prints matching counts and digest and the cutover files
tasks.title: S7: freeze the ledger, import it into a vault and cut over after a digest check

acceptance: When migrate --branch runs on a branch cut before the freeze, the tracker shall import its post-freeze ledger lines by event id and remove its ledger changes in one commit on that branch.
When a branch with .basicly/ledger changes lands on the code default branch after cutover, the next fsck --code shall import each new ledger line by event id.
When an imported event id is already valid in the vault, the import shall skip it.

Proof T-branch: input a branch cut before the freeze that appends to .basicly/ledger; action migrate --branch on it, then merge it; pass when the merge has no conflict and each line is in the vault once.
Proof T-late-ledger: input a branch merged after cutover that adds a new pending ledger shard; action fsck --code twice; pass when the first run imports each line once and the second imports nothing.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py migrate --branch --vault vault.git` on a pre-freeze branch prints the imported count and leaves one commit with no ledger change
tasks.title: S7: import a late branch's ledger lines with migrate --branch and fsck --code

acceptance: When migrate --rollback runs with --confirm and the prefix after cutover, the tracker shall push ended with reason rolled-back to the registry first, then to the vault, then export the vault events into the ledger and check the digest.
When a rerun follows a crash after the registry push, migrate --rollback shall continue at the vault push.
When the registry or the vault holds a valid ended event, every share shall stop, keep the queue and print the ended reason and the next command.
Proof T-rollback: input a cut-over fixture vault and registry; action migrate --rollback --confirm with the prefix; pass when both hold ended and the ledger fold equals the vault fold.

Proof T-ended: input 3 clones with queued events; action rollback crashes after the registry push, then every clone runs sync; pass when every clone stops sharing at its next fetch, every queue is kept and no event lands after ended.
tasks.demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py migrate --rollback --confirm demo --vault vault.git` exits 0 and a later sync prints ended rolled-back and keeps the queue
tasks.title: S7: roll back a cutover and stop every share on an ended event

acceptance: When the bulk load script runs, it shall drive 52 sessions on 13 clones of a local bare vault, each writing 10 bulk events per hour and firing the prompt hook every 2 minutes for 70 minutes, and print p95 visibility from a reader clone that fires its hook every 30 s.
When the nightly claim load runs, it shall run the claim load script at full time for 6 runs of 70 minutes with seeds 1 to 6 and at least 1,000 claims.
Cutover of a ledger shall wait until T-migrate, T-rollback, T-branch, T-ended, T-bulk, T-visible, T-claim-load and P-claim are green.
Proof T-bulk: input 52 sessions on 13 clones, seed 1; action the bulk load script; pass when p95 visibility is at most 240 s and Stop on every session leaves every queue empty.

Proof T-claim-load: input 6 full-time runs, seeds 1 to 6; action the claim load script; pass when every claim ends 0 or 3 within 60 s, one holder per record, p99 at most 10 s, mean at most 6 push attempts per minute and the busiest minute at most 24.
tasks.demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/bulk_load.py --sessions 52 --machines 13 --minutes 70 --seed 1` prints p95 visibility at most 240 s
tasks.title: S7: measure bulk visibility and nightly claim load before cutover

acceptance: When the P-claim probe runs on this machine with the local gh login, it shall drive 13 clones of the private repository basicly-testbed-vault for 2 hours, with basicly-testbed as the code repository and basicly-testbed-registry as the registry, and print p99, pushes per minute, rate-limit responses and push latency against an idle baseline.
If the gh login or a testbed repository is missing, the probe shall refuse and print the command that fixes it.
The nightly CI job for P-claim shall stay skipped by name until a CI token exists, and its workflow edit shall land only with the owner's confirmation.

Proof P-claim: input 13 clones of basicly-testbed-vault for 2 hours; action the probe; pass when p99 is at most 10 s, the mean is at most 6 pushes per minute, there is no HTTP 429 or secondary rate limit and push latency is at most twice the idle baseline.
tasks.demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/probe_claim.py --vault basicly-testbed-vault --clones 13 --minutes 120` prints p99, pushes per minute and rate-limit count
tasks.title: S7: probe claims on the private GitHub testbed with P-claim

Only the adapter calls wall_clock: events.append for its default and cli._run, which passes the clock down; every vault function takes clock as a required parameter. test_every_caller_of_the_one_wall_clock_is_named freezes the callers as cli.py _run and events.py append. (2) refs/basicly/retracted/N in the local vault clone is confirmed as allowed under the four conditions: never pushed, no fact only in a ref after repair, listed by fsck and doctor, stated in the design.

Owner answers 2026-11-12, relayed by the orchestrator, 'approved': (1) topology: one vault holds one or more projects; the vault is the access boundary; the default is one vault per team; for the owner, one vault for basicly, handily and terminal. (2) Name: 'the vault'; the default repository name at init is backlog-vault. (3) Visibility: private by default. The orchestrator created backlog-vault under the owner's account, private and empty; nothing is pushed to it before the plan is accepted, and the first push is the real init with genesis. basicly-testbed-registry is removed by the owner; basicly-testbed-vault stays as the sandbox for the real-host proof with the owner's own git login until the basicly cutover is proven. No token exists and none will.

Orchestrator decision 2026-11-12: the vault cutover plan (9 slices, about 35 h) is accepted with changes. (1) Cutover keeps .basicly/ledger in place, frozen, with MOVED.md; every events.append write refuses with exit 2 and names the vault command; a late branch that appended to the old files merges cleanly and its lines are imported by event id (as decided on .43.22); the cutover commit adds tracker.toml and MOVED.md and changes no ledger file; CI reads the frozen ledger and the live check moves to session start. (2) The real-host proof on basicly-testbed-vault runs right after config and init, with the owner's own git login; git ls-remote of backlog-vault and basicly-testbed-vault is approved, read only. (3) Rehearsal: after migration, migrate the real basicly ledger into basicly-testbed-vault, run the digest check and the read view, and time the first read, before the cutover against backlog-vault; the first push to backlog-vault is the real genesis. (4) Up to 3 lanes; all of today's lane rules hold. (5) The cutover is a coordinated moment with a named time and a handover first; tell the orchestrator one slice ahead for handily and terminal. Requirements for pass conditions: no token, secret or provider call in the product path, proven by a grep test with a known-match control; standalone proven by installing the tracker package in a clean environment with no harness and running init, create, claim, close and a read against a local bare vault from a plain script; init asks for the git address of an empty repository, suggests backlog-vault, prints the proposed repository and main-branch permissions, and says what it will push before it pushes; branch protection on a private repository under the owner's GitHub plan is established by interface-facts before init promises it, and the tool's retraction check does not depend on host protection. Archive result basicly-af8bh74 accepted: the checkpoint is built after the basicly cutover with the five fixes, each with a proof test, the two-holder breaks with a test that fails first; batching the fold's git calls may come earlier.

Owner statement 2026-11-12, relayed by the orchestrator: 'i need it in some other enterprise projects as well, to replace stuff like beads, br, beans, and Jira, or we can even integrate it in jira. Jira integration is a secondary objective ... something for later version in the future.' No test Jira system exists on this machine. Effect on the current plan, with no new slice: (1) migration step 4 names each supported source (beads, br, beans and the basicly ledger) and proves each with a fixture; (2) any git host stays a hard requirement and a local bare repository is the reference host; no provider call; (3) the event format and CLI stay stable for a later sync adapter: record ids, status, holder and links readable from one documented command with JSON output. Jira integration is filed as a priority 4 feature.

acceptance: When a tracker command runs in a code repository whose .basicly/tracker.toml names a vault URL and a project prefix, the command shall use that vault and that prefix without a --vault flag.

When vault init runs, the tracker shall ask for the git address of an empty repository, suggest the name backlog-vault, print the proposed permissions for the repository and its main branch, and print the files it will push before it pushes them.
When vault init runs on a repository that already has a commit, the tracker shall refuse with exit 2 and name the repository.
When a claim runs against a vault with no genesis commit, the tracker shall answer that the vault has no genesis and print the init command, not that the vault is unreachable.
The vault and tracker kit modules shall contain no gh call and no host API URL; a test shall prove this with a grep that also finds a known match planted in a fixture.

acceptance: When the real-host proof runs on this machine with the owner's own git login, it shall initialize basicly-testbed-vault, race two claims on one record from two clones, share from both, and observe one rejected push, using no token and no provider call.
When the proof ends, it shall print each step's exit code, the winning holder and the push latency, and no record shall have two holders.

acceptance: When tracker.toml names a vault, create, update, close, comment, review, confirm and dep shall queue one vault line holding the ledger event, and shall not write to .basicly/ledger.
When tracker.toml names a vault, claim and unassign shall write the built vault claim events and answer with the built exit codes.
When create runs with a vault, the new id shall use the project prefix from tracker.toml.
When tracker.toml names no vault, every write shall behave as today.

acceptance: When tracker.toml names a vault, present_ledger shall return a ledger-format view that holds the vault's valid events in vault order, and session start, ready and the board shall read it unchanged.
When the view is built, each record's holder shall come from the vault fold, not from an assignee field event.
When the local vault clone is shallow, the view shall refuse by name and print the fetch command that fixes it.
When list or ready runs, the view shall show only records with the repository's prefix unless --all-projects is given.
When show runs with --json, it shall print each record's id, status, holder and links as documented JSON.

When migrate --to-vault runs on a beads, br or beans issues file, it shall import its records with their ids; a fixture for each source shall prove it.
When migrate --from-vault runs with a project prefix, it shall export that prefix's vault events in vault order into ledger files whose fold equals the vault view fold.
If the counts or the digest differ, migrate shall refuse and name both values.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a tracker command first needs a vault, the tracker shall clone it bare into the vault's folder under the machine state folder with mode 0700 and fetch with the refspec +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main.
- While one command fetches a clone, any other fetch of that clone shall wait on the clone's one fetch lock.
- If a fetch fails, the tracker shall retry it once, then use the last fetched state and print its age.
- When a fetch succeeds and every new first-parent commit passes vault-check, the tracker shall move refs/basicly/seen to the fetched head.
- Proof T-refspec: input a fixture bare vault and a fresh bare clone; action push one batch commit to the vault, then fetch; pass when refs/remotes/origin/main and refs/basicly/seen equal the new head.
- Proof T-fetch-lock: input one clone and two concurrent fetches, one stalled 5 s by an injected git runner; action run both; pass when neither prints cannot lock ref and the head ref never moves backwards.

payload.text: Design recorded before code: claim RECORD --vault V spends one 30 s deadline: ls-remote probe at min(5 s, remaining) (exit 5, nothing queued), fetch at the remaining time, fold: held by this session exit 7, by another exit 3 with the take command and no push; else queue the claim and run an urgent share until the deadline, then fold again: exit 0 first valid, 3 another landed first, 4 unsettled (--wait and --cancel come in .43.16). Any other error exits 6 with the traceback in the clone log folder. Fetch also keeps the valid events in valid.jsonl so a claim folds one local file, not the whole chain. The session comes from --session or BASICLY_TRACKER_SESSION; missing exits 1 with the fix.

T-claim-burst runs at one tenth of the stated time scale in tests: a 3 s deadline and a 4 s stalled fetch stand for 30 s and 40 s; the pass checks every answer within the deadline plus 1 s and one holder after a sync. T-exclusive uses 8 sessions in one clone plus 2 other clones. A race in the first writer.id creation (one process read the file before another wrote it) was found by T-exclusive and fixed with a write-then-link; the old code failed 1 of 36 concurrent starts.

- Proof T-link: input a code clone with two commits naming one record; action fsck --code twice; pass when the vault holds two link events after the first run and no new event after the second.

## Context
The vault migration must preserve valid tracker state while publishing canonical redacted events.
This record ships with basicly-gtb19bg.43.39 and basicly-gtb19bg.43.40 as cut B.
## Decisions
The Orchestrator decision of 2026-11-13 supersedes literal event-id preservation when payloads require changes. This is amendment C6.
Every record id remains unchanged. Unchanged payloads retain their event ids. Changed payloads receive valid deterministic ids.
F1 defines one-time import. After cutover, the redacted vault is authoritative. Normal operation never depends on a private map.
Determinism compares canonical ledger bytes and event ids. Git commit hashes depend on destination parents and are excluded.
F2 keeps old-to-new id mapping private, optional, and at an explicitly supplied path. There is no default repository location.
An unignored mapping destination is refused. Ignore files are never edited. Mapping contents and unredacted hashes never reach shared output.
Mapping entries identify changed fields and account for removed events. They contain no plaintext removed value.
A control proved that an old event id can confirm a hidden holder name from a short candidate list.
Preserve valid reviews and closed state. Never promote stale or invalid evidence. Preserve operational event references and account for history.
Report external event-id citations without rewriting commit history, changelog or documentation.
The reviewed prototype commits are 49afcf1d and cf70d665. Replace their invalid id preservation and view normalization.
The original source ledger remains untouched. Live cutover and release remain outside this build.
## Demonstration
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py migrate --to-vault --preview reports canonical counts and digest without writes.

Every source event shall be accounted for, operational event references shall resolve, and projected sequences shall be gapless.
Private mapping shall require an explicit ignored destination, remain optional, and never reach shared output or logs.
Repeated import of the same source into the same vault shall refuse without writing.
Preview of a ledger import shall report canonical counts and digest without changing files or fetching.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When the standalone tracker is installed without basicly, its packaged CLI shall initialize a local vault and create, claim, confirm, close and read a record.
- When an agent connects to the packaged MCP server, it shall discover typed tools and operate the existing tracker lifecycle with repository isolation and unchanged admission gates.
- When agent guidance is installed, user scope shall be the default, repository scope shall remain available, and standalone and harness guidance shall describe vault operation without obsolete local-ledger write instructions.

payload.value:
## Context

The owner requires a standalone tracker that agents can install and operate. Agent tools, instructions, skills and scripts must ship together. User installation is the default. Repository installation remains optional. The basicly harness can use the same tools.

## Scope

Reuse the installed tracker CLI, installer and plugin. Add a packaged stdio MCP adapter with explicit repository binding. Adapt shipped tracker guidance and catalog sources. Keep tracker business rules in existing admission and write paths.

## Plan

The implementation and consumer tests cover packaged CLI operation, MCP discovery and lifecycle, invalid input, repository isolation, installation scopes, guidance and harness compatibility.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: No new dependency. Never bypass tracker admission, claim settlement or confirmation. No automatic change to unrelated agent configuration. Never infer a target repository from a global default.

[session handover 2026-11-13] [new facts]
Cut D follows landed cut B and cut C2, basicly-bebeo6k. Do not start it tonight.

Custom-template records must remain reviewed and closed after import and independent export.
Removing or altering required wrapper template metadata must fail closed.

It has no remote and is never pushed. Report its path. Removal needs the owner unless an owning fixture cleans it.
Use the real WSL br 0.3.2 CLI, verified by the Orchestrator, to create every supported record type.
Include open, in-progress and closed records, dependencies, comments, labels and a parent with children.
Use another data set copied from burndown-chart/.beads/issues.jsonl. Its reported size was 702 lines from the Orchestrator.
Read that source only. Change nothing in burndown-chart. Keep the copy and scratch vault local.
For each data set, prove unchanged record ids, equal record counts and field accounting with explicit dropped-field reasons.
Also prove resolved dependencies and parent links, preserved closed state, unchanged fsck on the view, and repeat refusal.
File gaps as backlog records. Foreign-format gaps do not block switching the three basicly ledgers.
Beans remains sample-level evidence because no real store or WSL beans command was available to the Orchestrator.
Windows is outside this rehearsal.

Add the standalone lifecycle proof from .43.32 on a migrated ledger.
Create, claim, update, review, confirm, close and read a vault-born record and a migrated record.
Prove no local ledger write. This depends on cut C2.
The live cutover covers development, basicly and handily only. Terminal stays on the old ledger.
Establish whether development/.beads/issues.jsonl was already imported or still needs import. Do not guess from its existence.
The previous Orchestrator count was 40 lines; remeasure at rehearsal.
Publish and install the owner-approved release in all cutover repositories before switching them.

[runbook draft 2026-11-13 section 1 of 4]
This runbook is blocked on the final C2 consumer and old-tool safety reports.
Do not execute its live steps tonight.

The owner approved the conditional basicly release and development-only switch on 2026-11-13.
Basicly, handily and terminal keep their current trackers.
The owner selected a private backlog-vault and no private id map.
Old external references to reminted event ids cannot use a migration map after this switch.
Normal vault reads and writes need no map.

Before release or a live switch step, stop and ask the owner on any refusal, failed check or differing count.
Other work fixes the cause without weakening a gate.

The retained part 1 rehearsal measured these values before the planned consumer writes.
Run this command from `basicly.worktrees/codex-vault-cut-d` with the private fixture alias supplied through the environment.

```sh
python3 .scripts/rehearse_vault_migration.py --source-repo ../.. --out ../../.orchestrator/codex-1-cut-d --part part1
```

| Item | Measured value |
| --- | --- |
| Source records | 60 |
| Source events | 491 |
| Carried events | 491 |
| Reminted events | 45 |
| View and export events | 504 |
| Current reviews | 2 |
| Current confirmations | 4 |
| Closed records | 19 |
| Old beads ids already imported | 40 of 40 |
| Template checks passed | 6 |
| Source human holder events | 9 |
| Export integrity exit code | 0 |

The export includes derived holder events.
Independent imports produced identical canonical bytes.
The standalone preview and import digests agreed.
The saved copy stays frozen while the live workspace ledger can grow.
A differing live count requires the owner before publication.
The copied consumer control has one record and three source events.
Its marker and source ledger bytes remained unchanged during import.
The scratch root is `.orchestrator/codex-1-cut-d` relative to the workspace.
The vault is `vault-0.git` there.
Keep these folders until the owner approves their removal.

The proposed release version is `0.46.0` because the release adds migration capabilities.
This version is a planning choice, not a published release.
Cut B is pushed at `5f876ad7` with green required main CI and passing destination verification.
The D helper is pushed separately at `ba5e9d18` and is not on main.

1. Wait for cut B and cut C2 on main with green required CI.
   Run the final development-copy rehearsal from that main commit.
   Include record identities, event accounting, process evidence, template checks and the old beads comparison.
   Obtain codex-2's final lifecycle and legacy-consumer reports from the same landed source.
   Record the exact commits, commands, digests and counts here.
   Replace this draft's provisional values before showing the final runbook to the owner.

2. Prepare the release in its own tracked record and lane.
   Use the proposed version only after all required source and consumer checks pass.
   Add the release summary before the release command assembles its commit and tag.
   Land the notes through the normal lock and hooks.
   Wait for green required main CI.
   Use the primary basicly checkout for the release command, as its guard requires.
   The release commit refers to the completed rehearsal record.

   ```sh
   uv run basicly release 0.46.0 --issue basicly-gtb19bg.43.33 --dry-run
   uv run basicly release 0.46.0 --issue basicly-gtb19bg.43.33
   git push origin main
   git push origin v0.46.0
   ```

   Run each command separately and inspect its result before the next command.
   Keep the main lock through the main push and release it immediately afterward.
   Confirm the tag workflow and published release before installing the release in development.
   A release failure requires the owner before any further release action.

[runbook draft 2026-11-13 section 2 of 4]
3. Upgrade the shared WSL engine, then install its kit in development only.
   The Orchestrator selected this order because daily commands use the global engine.
   Other repositories keep their installed kits and local trackers.
   Their `basicly check` version-skew result still needs the candidate comparison report.
   Tracker commands and commit hooks must pass that comparison before this step.
   The Windows global tool stays unchanged.
   The released old kit and engine must refuse safely or read correctly against the switched scratch repository.
   A silent local write or changed vault configuration blocks the live switch.

   From the workspace, first record the clean base commit and acquire its coordination lock.
   The workspace installation task must be filed, reviewed and claimed before managed-file writes.

   ```sh
   development_before_vault=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
   uv tool install --python '>=3.14' --force https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/releases/download/v0.46.0/basicly-0.46.0-py3-none-any.whl
   basicly --version
   basicly install --dry-run
   basicly install
   basicly check
   basicly hooks-check
   ```

   Expected version is `0.46.0`.
   Inspect the dry-run paths before installation.
